# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-NODE-1-JOIN

## Summary
`phm node join | status | leave` (all with `--json`). Join reuses the machine's own
`gh` login (`gh api user --jq .login`; only the validated login is read, never a token),
registers the node in the existing drive lease store (`src/core/drive/nodes`, under
`$ASHLR_HOME/nodes`), advertises caps, and starts a detached heartbeat (10 s renew of the
30 s lease; exits by itself once the session is revoked/replaced/expired).

- Node record now carries `meta: {owner:{kind:person|team|org,id}, ghUser, caps}`
  (optional field on `NodeRecord`, validated in `parseState`; old state still parses).
  Default owner = `person:<gh user>`, no prompts; `--owner kind:id` overrides.
- Caps: arch, cpus, memGiB, node, os and sorted tools found on PATH (no process spawns).
- `join` idempotent (`already-joined`); `leave` idempotent (`not-joined`); `status` exits 0
  when not joined and names the next command in `fix`. Errors are `error:` + `fix:`
  (or `{error,fix}` in JSON).
- Docs: `docs/NODE-JOIN.md` (plain English + copy-paste), `docs/llms.txt`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/cli.md`, help registry, completions.

## Deviations / limits (honest)
- RQ-NODECAPS-14 and a "fleetlease"/gh-auth heartbeat module are NOT in this checkout; the
  only lease store present is `src/core/drive/nodes` (RQ-DRIVER-NODES-1-LEASE), so I built on
  that and wrote a minimal caps probe. Swap `detectCaps` for NODECAPS-14 when it lands.
- The registry is the single-host local store, so "shared fleet" = all nodes using the same
  `~/.ashlr/nodes`. No repo-backed/multi-host registry yet (documented in NODE-JOIN.md);
  the record schema (owner, caps) is what a remote registry would carry.
- Heartbeat does not survive reboot; `status` reports `expired` with the fix `phm node join`.
- No UI, so no screenshot. Real `gh` / detached-spawn path is not exercised in tests (injected);
  not run against a live gh login.
- Size: ~160 LOC core + ~50 CLI, plus tests/docs; total net ≈ +377 (over the 250 target once

# BRIDGE_NOTES — RQ-GUARDIANHEADQ8

## Summary

`fleet guardian-verify` can now verify a repository's observed remote head
without a hand-written manifest. The new `--head-of <absolute repo path>` flag
(optional `--branch <name>`, exclusive with `--manifest`) resolves
`refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` — or the `origin/HEAD` symref when `--branch` is
omitted — through local `execFile` git reads only (never a fetch), takes the
head commit's first parent as `baseHead`, and synthesizes a one-entry manifest
whose `cohortId`/`proposalId` are `guardian-<sha12(head)>`. The manifest is
written atomically (`O_EXCL` temp file, mode `0o600`, rename) under
`os.tmpdir()`, handed to the unchanged verification loop, and unlinked after
success or error. Refusals: relative/non-absolute paths, non-repo directories
(including repo subdirectories — `rev-parse --show-toplevel` must realpath to
the given path), syntactically invalid or unresolvable branch names, missing
`origin/HEAD` with no `--branch`, and parentless (root-commit) heads.
`guardian-verify-loop.ts` and `detached-post-merge-runner.ts` are untouched.

## Changes

- `src/core/fleet/guardian-head-manifest.ts` (NEW): `GuardianHeadError`,
  `buildGuardianHeadEntry(repo, branch?)`, `runGuardianHeadVerification(options)`
  with `GuardianHeadOptions extends Omit<GuardianOptions, 'manifest'>` plus
  `repo`/`branch`/`loop` seams. Async `execFile` git reads with a scrubbed env
  (`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_CONFIG_*` family removed, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `LC_ALL=C`, no network verbs).
- `src/cli/fleet-guardian-verify.ts`: accepts `--head-of`/`--branch`; exits 2 on
  flag-shape errors (`--head-of`+`--manifest`, `--branch` without `--head-of`,
  missing/duplicate values), 3 on refusals surfaced from the core module;
  `--help`/`-h` print usage and exit 0 per repo convention. The existing `run`
  injection seam doubles as the loop seam for `--head-of`.
- `test/fleet-guardian-head-manifest-01.test.ts` (NEW): 10 tests over real temp
  git repos; the detached runner is always stubbed, so no real profile ever runs.
- `test/config/realio-lane-membership.mjs`: registered the new suite (it spawns
  real `git` children).

## Commands run

- `npm ci` (restored a partial `node_modules` — eslint `lib/` was absent)
- `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` — PASS (file selection, fleet registry,
  eslint changed files, tsgo --noEmit, realio lane, verse sync-I/O)

- `npx eslint <touched files>` — clean
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-guardian-head-manifest-01.test.ts`
  — 10/10 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-guardian-verify-loop-01.test.ts
  test/fleet-guardian-total-deadline-02.test.ts
  test/fleet-verb-registry-repair-01.test.ts` — 16/16 pass
- `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/fleet-verb-convention.test.ts
  test/fleet-subcommand-registry.test.ts test/doc-facts.test.ts
  test/docs-fleet-verbs.test.ts` — 137 tests pass; `docs-fleet-verbs.test.ts`
  reports vitest "No test suite found" — a pre-existing quirk of that file's
  `node:test` imports, unrelated to this change (its 25 checks printed green).

## Pass/fail counts

- New suite: 10/10. Touched-area suites: 16/16. Verb/doc surfaces: 137/137.
- verify-changed: all PASS; check:docs: clean; eslint on touched files: clean.

+419: `guardian-head-manifest.ts` +181, `fleet-guardian-head-manifest-01.test.ts`

## Summary

`ashlr fleet safari-import <status|begin-import>` — a bounded convention verb
that bridges `scripts/mac-bridge/safari_import.py` (merged, previously
uncalled) into the fleet CLI, so an agent can check or open Safari's built-in
File > Import From > Google Chrome dialog. Any block lands in
`<root>/supervisor/NEEDS-MASON.md`, which the verb always passes as an
absolute `--needs-mason` path (never the script's cwd-relative default).

Modeled on the sibling `src/cli/fleet-app.ts` (RQ-PHX-FLEETAPPVERB01) merged
upstream during this job: same exec seam shape (`exec(file, argv, options)`
rejecting on nonzero/kill), same `locateScript` dep with a package.json-bounded
walk up from `import.meta.url`, same console/`vi.spyOn` test style.

Behavior:
- `python3 -I <script> <mode> --needs-mason <abs> --timeout <n>` via execFile,
  never a shell; mode validated against {status, begin-import} before spawn.
- `--timeout` finite, 1–120, default 15; child killed at timeout + 15s
  (execFile `timeout` option, SIGKILL).
- `--root` default `~/.ashlr-runs`; relative roots resolved absolute.
- Exit 2 on bad args with usage; exit 1 + one clear "needs a Phantom source
  checkout" line when the script is absent (npm package never ships scripts/;
  package.json "files" unchanged); exec seam default is injectable.
- Helper's one JSON object on stdout is the contract. `--json` writes stdout
  unchanged and propagates the exit code (2 = blocked, a normal result).
  Non-json prints one human line: blocked lines carry `blocked.reason`,
  `blocked.detail`, the noted NEEDS-MASON path and `nextAction`; success lines
  describe mechanics only — `import confirmed`/`websites signed in` print only

title: Run hosted test CI once a day
body:
## What & why Hosted test CI was starting on every pull request. Those runs mail `PR run failed: CI` (for example `CI - bridge: RQ-PHX-PHONEQRCODE31`) when the PR head tree differs from GitHub's synthetic merge commit. The merge queue already had a short gate. This change stops per-PR and per-push test CI, keeps that queue gate, and makes the daily run cheaper. Rulesets, billing, and secrets are unchanged. The required check is still **Merge Gate** (GitHub Actions). It still reports on `merge_group`, which is what the merge queue waits for. ### Triggers | Workflow | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) | `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `workflow_call`, daily `3 9 * * *`, `workflow_dispatch` | `merge_group`, `workflow_call`, daily `3 9 * * *`, `workflow_dispatch`. No `pull_request`. | | Dependency Audit | every PR, path-filtered `push` to master, weekly `17 9 * * 1`, `workflow_dispatch` | weekly `17 9 * * 1` and `workflow_dispatch` only | | PR topology | `pull_request_target` on every PR event, plus `workflow_dispatch` | daily idle at `23 9 * * *` (no install), and `workflow_dispatch` to inspect one PR | | Release, auto-tag, custody, companion smoke, merge-queue reaper | unchanged | unchanged. Tag and release pushes stay. The reaper stays on its 30-minute schedule so it can cancel orphaned merge-queue runs; it is not a test suite. | ### What still runs, and how long **Merge queue (every queued commit).** Secret-shape scan, lane classify, and a quick `tsc --noEmit`, then Merge Gate. A green queue run on 2026-11-02 took about **80 seconds** on Ubuntu (run 41381447556). macOS and Windows stay skipped. Agents still run `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` before merge; that is documented in `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. It does not replace Merge Gate. **Daily CI at 09:03 UTC, plus `workflow_dispatch`.** Ubuntu authority shards (3, parallel), Windows portability (4, parallel), Windows service authority, one rotated Mac isolated slice, the shared macOS queue lane, and the native broker. npm caching on `setup-node` is unchanged. The four-way **Mac general** matrix no longer runs on the schedule. It repeats the Ubuntu suites on `macos-15` (about 10× a Linux minute; the 2026-11-01 slice took ~14 minutes and was the expensive daily leg). `workflow_dispatch` still runs it (`mac_shard=all`, or `0`–`6` for one slice). **Expected daily wall clock: about 15–20 minutes.** On the last green full run (2026-10-26) the Ubuntu shards were ~7–15 minutes and Windows ~6–12 minutes, in parallel with Mac isolated (~7–18 minutes), shared macOS (~2 minutes), and the broker (~5 minutes). That day also ran all four Mac general shards and the workflow lasted about four hours. Dropping Mac general from the schedule removes that queue. **Dependency audit** stays weekly (already at most once a day) so it does not add a second daily Ubuntu job. Its clean-install contract still refuses an npm cache. ### Why the daily run was red The 2026-11-01 scheduled run failed before the suites: - `.github/CODEOWNERS` had drifted from the owner-lane renderer (104 Tier-1 test paths). Regenerated. - `test/fixtures/authority/tier1-closure.json` did not include new Tier-1 roots (`src/core/routing/arms.ts`, `src/core/routing/bandit.ts`, `src/core/verse/outcomes-api.reissue.test.ts`, which matches the existing `outcomes-*.ts` pattern) or the import closure that grew with them. Regenerated. This records the current closure; later growth still fails the test. - `test/documentation-navigation.test.ts` and `config set --help` already pass on current master (fixed after that red run in #2647 and #2661). The full Ubuntu/Windows/Mac suites were not re-run here. A later case in those shards can still fail the next daily run. ## How it was verified - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` - `npm run check:docs` - `npx eslint` on the three edited test files - `HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/m30.ci.test.ts test/m440.dependency-audit-ci.test.ts test/m484.pr-topology-admission.test.ts test/authority-codeowners-310b.test.ts test/authority-tier1-closure-310b.test.ts test/documentation-navigation.test.ts test/m33.release-meta.test.ts test/m481.ci-action-pins.test.ts test/config-set-help-exit.test.ts test/doc-facts.test.ts test/m468.release-desktop-workflow-policy.test.ts` Not run: `npm run lint` (full tree), `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck:web`, or the hosted matrix. ## Notes - No new dependencies. No ruleset, billing, or secret changes. - `toolsUsed`: none of the Phantom companion MCP servers.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **CI** * Pull requests and branch pushes no longer start hosted CI. The full suite runs on its daily schedule or by manual dispatch, while merge-queue commits continue to run the quick gate. * The exhaustive Mac general test matrix now runs only by manual dispatch. * Dependency-audit and topology workflows now run on schedules or by manual dispatch, rather than on pull requests. * **Documentation** * Updated contributor guidance to reflect CI triggers and pre-merge checks.

`phm land auto` runs one bounded sweep over the fleet's open PRs (the
fleet-merge-state records under `~/.ashlr/authority/fleet-merge`), reads each
live from GitHub, classifies it, and — under `--apply` — acts:

| class | meaning | action under `--apply` |
|---|---|---|
| `green-ready` | required checks green, mergeable | none (the standing pass lands it) |
| `behind` | `mergeable_state: behind` or the live base head moved past the recorded base | `updateFleetPrBranch` → GitHub `PUT /pulls/<n>/update-branch` (merge method only; the REST endpoint has no rebase), pinned to the classified head SHA |
| `conflicting` | `mergeable`/state says the PR conflicts | enqueues a DRAIN task ("Land PR #n … resolve merge conflicts", routes as the land-first `land` class) |
| `red-required` | G7 sees a required check fail | enqueues a FIXUP task (routes `fixup`) naming the first failing required check |
| `pending` | required checks still running | none |
| `blocked` | draft/review/checks-timeout | none |
| `closed` / `moved` / `held` / `unknown` | merged or closed, head drifted, owner-lane/hold/unledgered/non-fleet author, or unreadable GitHub | none — fail closed |

- Dry-run by default; `--apply` additionally requires `PHANTOM_MERGE_AUTOPILOT=1`

  only GitHub effect in the sweep is `PUT update-branch` (`updateFleetPrBranch`

- Hold list honored via `listRepoHolds` (quarantine.ts); an unreadable hold
  store fails the entire run closed — it also refuses before any GitHub read.
- Per-PR cap of 3 actions inside a rolling 24 h window, remembered on the
  merge-state record itself (`autopilot` memo, validated, bounded at 32 rows);
  a lost memo write is reported in the action detail rather than silently
  undercounting. Dry-run reports the cap as `skipped`, not `planned`.
- Required-check semantics reuse G7 exactly (`evaluateG7Checks`; the run/status
  → state mapping is now exported, so `firstFailingRequiredCheck` cannot
  diverge). Local-enforcement repos skip the rulesets read they never use.
- GitHub errors, malformed responses, unreadable state records and unreadable

# RQ-BUS-1C bridge notes

Implemented `phm bus send|inbox|ack --json`, including real cross-process local
mailbox persistence, strict argument validation, help, completion and agent docs.
All changes remain uncommitted on `codex-bridge/RQ-BUS-1C`, based on `a6f3c323`.

## Scope and dependency decision

The supplied default-branch worktree had no durable bus send/inbox/ack core.
The available sibling bus branches did not provide one either. To deliver a
working command rather than a mock adapter, this change adds
`src/core/fleet/bus-mailbox.ts`, using Phantom's existing immutable private-record
store. No separate persistence framework or runtime dependency was introduced.

`src/core/fleet/bus-envelope.ts` and `schema/bus.v1.schema.json` are byte-identical
to RQ-BUS-1A at `06e834ebbe67af96f025b299fcb62793bb1f6e4a` (verified with Git blob
hashes). They are included as uncommitted source dependencies, without merging
or modifying that branch. The existing fleet lifecycle pub/sub API is unchanged.

## Behavior

- Send accepts an opaque JSON body, sender/recipient labels, optional stable ID,
  P0-P3 priority and positive safe-integer TTL in milliseconds. Defaults: UUID,
  P2, 300000 ms. Same ID and identical envelope deduplicate without renewing TTL;
  changing the envelope under that ID refuses.
- Inbox is read-only, returns pending/unexpired messages by priority then local
  acceptance time, reports remaining TTL and `hasMore`, and never acknowledges.
- Ack verifies the stored recipient and is idempotent, including after expiry.
  Unknown IDs and mismatched recipients refuse without creating acknowledgments.
- JSON mode emits one object on stdout for success or failure. Exit codes:
  0 success, 1 operational refusal, 2 invalid usage. Diagnostics do not echo
  raw arguments, JSON parser errors, payloads or filesystem error paths.
- Supports `--option=value` and `ack --to <label> [--json] -- <literal-id>` so
  flag-shaped labels/IDs round-trip. Help performs no work.
- Uses hashed record identities, private directories/files, immutable publication,
  bounded reads and shared store locks/recovery. Malformed, unsafe or changing
  storage refuses rather than appearing empty. Missing inbox reads create nothing.
- Admission caps history at 5000 messages / 64 MiB, reserving acknowledgment
  slots and bytes under the publication lock. At capacity, existing inboxes,
  exact retries and acknowledgments remain available. Crash recovery finalizes
  already-linked records even when new traffic is refused. No history is deleted.
- Rejects credential-shaped values using the existing scrubber. Secret-shaped
  test data is constructed at runtime and marked FAKE.

This is a same-OS-user local transport. Routing labels are not authenticated
principals. Remote provider delivery, RQ-EVENTD wake-up, bus hop logging and
execution authority are separate integrations; this command does not invoke them.

RQ-QUEUE-5: live station graph for the Phantom desktop web UI, fed by `queue.stats.v1`.

## What
- `src/web-ui/data/queue-stats/schema.ts`: typed `queue.stats.v1` schema, validator, rho bands, bottleneck selection. No React import, so RQ-QUEUE-3 (`phm queue stats --json`) can import it and emit exactly this shape.
- `fixtures.ts`: normal, overloaded and empty payloads.
- `source.ts`: pluggable adapter. `fixture` works now; `command` (stub for `phm queue stats --json`) and `http` (stub for a same-origin route) return the same parsed result.
- `QueueStationGraph.tsx`: plain SVG, one node per station in pipeline order, filled by rho band, labeled with rho and queue length, bottleneck outlined. Refreshes on an interval (default 15 s). Mounted in Fleet Dashboard.
- `agent-workspace-flag.ts`: minimal local gate.

## Decisions and reasons
- Flag: `agentWorkspace` is not on master yet (RQ-DESKTOP-P1-1 in flight). This PR gates locally with `localStorage["phantom.flag.agentWorkspace"] === "1"`, default off, in one function so it can switch to the P1-1 flag store with a one-line change. Flag off renders nothing, so the UI is unchanged.
- Rho thresholds: green < 0.7, amber 0.7 to < 0.9, red >= 0.9 (and non-finite). At rho 0.7 M/M/1 wait is about 2.3x service time and at 0.9 it is 9x, growing without bound toward 1.
- Bottleneck: highest rho, ties broken by largest `queueGrowthPerHour`, then earliest station for determinism. Idle input (no stations, or all rho 0 with empty queues) gives none.
- Redaction: the parser copies only whitelisted fields, station ids must be in the known enum, and pool ids must be short slugs that do not look like credentials. Unknown keys never reach the DOM.
- No dependency added; plain SVG. No CODEOWNERS or Tier-1 paths touched (all changes in src/web-ui/data and src/web-ui/routes/fleet-dashboard).

## Schema `queue.stats.v1`
```ts
{
  schema: 'queue.stats.v1';
  generatedAt: string;            // ISO
  windowSec: number;              // > 0
  stations: Array<{ station: 'planned'|'ready'|'claimed'|'pr_ci'|'merge_queue'|'merged'|'publish'|'released'|'fix_main' } & Metrics>;
  pools: Array<{ pool: string /* slug */ } & Metrics>;
  little: { drift: boolean; ratio: number };   // drift when |L - lambda*W|/L > 0.2
}
Metrics = { lambda, mu, rho, queueLength, waitSec, wip: number >= 0; queueGrowthPerHour: number }
```

title: feat(custody): carry spawn custody into receipt secrets.wrap; hold needs-secrets tasks that would run unwrapped
body:
## What
Custody step 2 (design-custody-fleet.md 3.2), handed to us by Phantom Core.
1. **Receipt `secrets.wrap` is filled from the real spawn decision.** It used to be always `null`. Each daemon dispatch now runs inside a per-item custody capture. Every `spawnEngine` call in that dispatch reports its custody record there, next to the existing `onCustody` callback. At run close the daemon passes the result to `emitReceiptForDispatchEvent`.
2. **Hold rule:** a work item tagged `needs-secrets` never spawns unwrapped. If the custody decision is unwrapped (for any reason: phantom disabled, not initialized, worktree namespace, self-authenticating engine, preflight blocked or unavailable), `spawnEngine` returns `ok: false` with `held: task needs secrets but the spawn would run unwrapped (<reason>)` before the child starts.

## Why each decision
- **AsyncLocalStorage capture instead of threading `onCustody` through every layer.** The daemon reaches `spawnEngine` through runGoal, the orchestrator, sandboxed-engine and other adapters (11 call sites of `spawnEngine`). Threading a callback through all of them would touch many unrelated files. A scope opened in `loop.ts` around `runItem` reaches every spawn for that item, including nested ones. The `onCustody` option is kept and still called. Concurrent items are isolated (tested).
- **The wrap is passed in memory, not added to the dispatch ledger event.** The ledger has a strict persisted schema and validators. Adding a field there would be a schema change outside this step. The receipt is emitted in the same tick that holds the capture, so no persistence is needed.
- **Aggregation: any unwrapped spawn means the receipt says unwrapped, with the first unwrapped reason; all wrapped means wrapped; no spawn means null.** A run with even one spawn outside custody was not fully under custody, so claiming `wrapped: true` would overstate. `null` keeps "unknown" distinct from "no".
- **Declaration is the exact work item tag `needs-secrets`.** `WorkItem.tags` already exists. A tag needs no type or ledger change and is easy to set from any work source. Matching is exact and case-sensitive, so a near-miss tag never changes behavior silently.
- **The hold sits in `spawnEngine`, right after the custody record is written.** That way the record of the unwrapped decision still lands (step 1 ledger plus status), the refusal names the reason, and no child process starts. Per 3.2, self-authenticating CLIs (claude, codex) are unwrapped by design, so a `needs-secrets` task routed to them is held too. That is the intended conservative behavior.
- **Off by default in practice:** nothing changes unless an item carries the tag. Receipts still require `ASHLR_RUN_RECEIPTS=1`.
- **No CHANGELOG line yet:** #914 adds a line at the same spot. I will add one after #914 merges to avoid a conflict.

## Tier-1 self-review
Touches Tier-1 files `src/core/run/engines.ts` and `src/core/daemon/loop.ts`, plus receipt code (`receipt-dispatch.ts`, Core's area, edited only for this step). The new module `src/core/run/custody-capture.ts` joins the Tier-1 closure through the official regen (`ASHLR_UPDATE_TIER1_CLOSURE=1`, +1 line). CODEOWNERS gets +1 line, `/test/custody-wrap-receipt.test.ts`, via `ASHLR_UPDATE_CODEOWNERS=1`. Both are pre-approved growth with no removals. No narrowing of Tier-1, CODEOWNERS or rulesets.
- engines.ts: additive. The only new behavior is an early refusal when a scope asks for wrap and the spawn is unwrapped. Without a scope (all non-daemon callers) `custodyRequiresWrap()` is false, so nothing changes. The hold can only make a spawn stricter, never looser.
- loop.ts: wraps `runItem` in the capture scope and passes the wrap to receipt emission. No change to dispatch, ledger writes or outcome handling.
- receipt-dispatch.ts: the new optional `wrap` parameter defaults to `null` (old behavior). The body is still checked by `isReceiptV1Body`, which already enforces wrapped/reason consistency.
- Value-free: the capture holds only custody records (flag, fixed reason code, engine basename, preflight exit), capped at 64 per dispatch, in memory.
- Risk: an item tagged `needs-secrets` that used to run unwrapped will now fail as held. That is the point of the rule. Revert: revert the squash commit. Second-agent review recommended (non-blocking).
